### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b2b7b210300e2b73c98bac8b7f16988a86a36bf6` — the merge of head `b3af029a091d7728d2d51f9c27426f82f94415b4` into base `5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin b2b7b210300e2b73c98bac8b7f16988a86a36bf6 && git checkout b2b7b210300e2b73c98bac8b7f16988a86a36bf6
```

### ① Derived judgments

**Exit 1, `expandRelatedRecords` — right, at every depth and from every entry point.** The new branch (`engine.ts:13001`) sits after the three pure checks the loop already made (`fieldDef`, `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`, `referenceTargetOf`) and before any id is collected (`allIds`, 13004) or any `find` is issued, so a target the family predicate names is never the subject of a sub-read. A repository-wide grep finds exactly three callers: the recursion, `find` (14112) and `findOne` (14399); no write response expands. Every door that carries an expand tree reaches one of those two: the data door's list read (`protocol.ts:14501-14507`, after `assertExpandTargetsExist` and `servedExpand`), its single read (`14922-14934`, into `engine.findOne`), an action's data read (`action-execution.ts:390`, through the door), the import runner (`import-runner.ts:164`, into `engine.find`), the hook body's `ctx.api` repository facade (`body-runner.ts:1075`, options passed through to `ql.find`), and the nested form (`fillQueryAstDefaults`, 13900-13912, rebuilds the nested map the loop recurses into). The MCP package declares no expand option on any tool; its stdio bridge is engine-only and names expand only as something the HTTP layer has (`stdio-data-bridge.ts:50`) — the dev's "not an entry point" is exact. The data door's projection is unchanged and still keyed on the requested object only (`redactStoredMetadataRows`, `protocol.ts:14796`; `redactStoredMetadataRow`, 14942), as the claim required.

**What the field answers, and that it discloses nothing — right.** `continue` leaves `record[fieldName]` untouched: the stored id, for a single and a multiple-valued reference alike. The branch runs before any read, so an existing, an absent and a forbidden family row answer byte-identically, and identically to the two answers the loop already gives — the door's `servedExpand` dropping an unexposed target (#22661, id kept) and the loop's own `catch` retaining the id after a refused sub-read. The door's expand gate (`assertExpandTargetsExist`, `protocol.ts:13419-13469`) still admits the field (it exists, is a reference, has a target), so the response is the ordinary 200 with the bare id and nothing names the target. The only observable difference from before is the absence of the warn log a refused sub-read used to leave, which no caller receives. The engine pin's `familyReads()` counts every driver call on the family table and asserts 0 for the expand cases under a member and under SYSTEM; `servesNothing` asserts no placeholder reaches any result; nested depth 1, `findOne` with a projection naming the two protected columns, and the multiple-valued reference are all driven.

**Exit 2, the `parent` root — right, in all three binders, for every caller.** `resolveMasterDetailParent` (9762): the guard at 9777 follows `resolveMasterDetailRelation` and precedes `masterIdOf`, read 1 (`masterDetailHeadersCallerReads`) and read 2 (the elevated whole-row `findOne`). `resolveMasterDetailParents` (9826): the guard at 9837 returns the `unbound` closure before any id is collected. `resolvePreviewParents` (9914): the guard is folded into the condition at 9935, so neither its read 1 (a caller-context whole-row `find` on the master, 9939-9942) nor its read 2 runs, and `headerOf` answers `null` for every id. Each guard sits ahead of the `context?.isSystem` short-circuit inside `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` (9572), so a SYSTEM caller — which previously went straight to read 2 — is refused exactly as a member is; the pin runs every case under both. The callers are the insert (15949, gated on `hasParentScopedRequiredWhen`), the by-id update (17437 through `settleMasterDetailLanding.resolve`, 17457 for the repoint's previous header), the bulk update (17739, 17751) and the preview (14956); `settleMasterDetailLanding` (9665) reads only `rel.fk` off the relation. With `parent` unbound, a `requiredWhen` is unevaluable and the write is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` and the fixed text at `rule-validator.ts:3957-3960`, which names the slot and the field and never the row; a `readonlyWhen` is LOCKED (`master-detail.ts` header, #4889), so the field is stripped identically whatever the header holds. The pin asserts the insert refusal is `toEqual` across the holding and the control header, the update answers are equal, and the preview's two outputs differ only by the header id. No verdict depends on the row.

**The family reads a detail write still makes — id-only, right.** The write's reference check (`assertReferencesResolve`, 9394-9480) asks, for a `master_detail`, `masterDetailHeaderExists`: the caller's read door projected to `id` (`masterDetailHeadersCallerReads`, `fields: ['id']`), then `referenceExists` (elevated, `fields: ['id']`). A caller whose door does not return the family header gets `reference_not_found` whether or not the row exists — the same bit the family's own door gives that caller — and nothing beyond `id` is ever materialised. The pin's `familyBodyReads()` permits exactly an `id`-only read and asserts 0 others. Right, and consistent with the dev's explanation of #24316's "refused as unbound" (the caller read door, #22519).

**Every other place a reference target is read by id — searched, none unguarded.** `referenceTargetOf` has exactly three call sites in `engine.ts`: 9452 (the write's existence probe, id-only), 10135 (`resolveOneHopRelated`, guarded at 10145 by PR #24344's branch, `69147abf25`, which is in this PR's base and precedes that loader's own `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` call at 10233) and 12991 (this exit). `resolveFileReferences` reads `sys_file` only. A hook body's `ctx.title()` related read (`body-runner.ts:291`) goes through the body api, where a family object is refused as a subject by `storedMetadataBodyReadRefusal` (`stored-metadata-body-boundary.ts:131`, applied at `stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts:185/241/319`). plugin-security's by-id reads (`fetchRecord` 5023, the pre-image 7042, `checkAuthoredRowWrite` 5474) read the addressed object, never a reference target, and its controlled-by-parent derivation reads master ids only (4180). No binder or hydration that reads a family row whole by reference remains in the engine or the doors read.

**Non-family references unchanged on both exits — right.** Both guards key on `isStoredMetadataBodyObject` alone, the one membership set (`STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS`, two tables, `stored-metadata-body-objects.ts:47-54`; no second list). The pin drives an ordinary lookup on the same carrier (`other`, still served as the related object) and an ordinary master (`probe_ordinary_detail`, whose `requiredWhen` over the header is still judged: refused without the field, accepted with it, the refusal not the unbound-parent text). `resolveMasterDetailRelation` (`master-detail.ts:220`) is unchanged, so the relation's other reader keeps its answer, as the PR says.

**The family pin — right.** `FAMILY_SURFACES` 26 → 28 (8 original + 15 of #21207 + 3 of #24316 + 2 here, counted). Each new row names its owning pin, `@objectstack/objectql (engine-hydration-stored-metadata-body.test.ts)`, the file this PR adds, with dispositions `withheld` (the id is kept) and `refuses` (no verdict), both in the pin's vocabulary. The header's per-package list gains the same pin. The surfaces the rows name — the carrying object's data read in both expand spellings and the nested form, `findOne`, a hook body's `ctx.api` read; `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen` on insert and update, the `validate()` preview — are exactly the drives the engine pin makes, and together with #24316's three rows the enumeration now names every exit the card and this record name.
